items.title: Nepal needs the world. But Nepal must build Nepal.
items.summary: The recent floods in Rasuwa have once again reminded us how vulnerable Nepal remains to disasters. Families have lost homes and livelihoods. Infrastructure has been damaged. Communities are waiting for relief and, beyond that, the long and difficult process of recovery and reconstruction. At a time like this, the generosity of people, organisations and countries […] The post Nepal needs the world.

items.title: The flood was natural, but was the disaster?
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi flash flood in Nepal cannot simply be called a natural disaster. Extreme floods are commonly described using annual exceedance probabilities or return periods—such as 50-, 100- or 500-year events, or even rarer ones. items.title: They stopped hoping to find him alive. Then they found a hand
items.summary: Raj Kumar Diyali went missing with his wife and four-year-old son in Nepal’s Bhotekoshi flood. His family is now waiting for DNA confirmation.

items.title: Barely saved, he cuts mourning short to help flood survivors
items.summary: Sudip Kumar Neupane watched a raging Trishuli swallow his younger brother and a close colleague, then came out of grief after two days.

items.title: Can Nepal turn Himalayan vulnerability into a case for compensation?
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi disaster highlights rising climate risks in the Himalayas, but experts say Nepal needs stronger evidence, sharper diplomacy and a clear strategy to secure international grants.

items.title: After nine days in darkness, two men walked back into the light
items.summary: Rescuers pulled Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan alive from the Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel after more than 72 hours of painstaking search, but dozens of people remain unaccounted for.

items.title: Search and rescue team says ‘no more survivors in Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel’
items.summary: After rescuing two survivors and finding a dead body, rescuers say they could not locate any more survivors or bodies.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 1,287
items.summary: Bodies have been recovered across eight districts, with Chitwan reporting the highest number of bodies at 359, followed by Nawalparasi East and Nawalparasi West.

items.title: Rescued tunnel worker says he stayed behind to save others
items.summary: Sanjay Sah told rescuers he delayed his escape to help others flee after the flood struck the Trishuli 3A tunnel, leaving him trapped inside for nine days.

items.title: Wife says rescued husband has ‘a second life’ after nine days trapped in Nepal tunnel
items.summary: Hira Shobha said her family spent nine agonising days believing Kabir Maharjan was still alive inside the Trishuli 3A tunnel before rescuers pulled him out on Friday.

items.title: Nepal flood survivors pulled alive from hydropower tunnel nine days later
items.summary: The rescue of two men came after rescuers heard voices from inside the Trishuli 3A tunnel, raising hopes that others trapped since the August 26 disaster may still be alive.

items.title: Nepal unveils relief package to help flood-hit businesses recover
items.summary: Customs and tax breaks, loan restructuring and cheaper credit offered to businesses affected by Bhotekoshi floods.

items.title: 600 children unaccounted for in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. Verification hampered by crippled communication
items.summary: 12 schools—four in Rasuwa and eight in Nuwakot—were completely destroyed in the August 26 mid-morning disaster.

items.title: The priest leading his people from grief to acceptance
items.summary: In a Rasuwa village, grieving families have begun performing Buddhist funeral rites without waiting for bodies, following the lead of chief priest Singi Lama, who lost his son and daughters-in-law in the disaster.

items.title: Nepal weighing options to relocate Bhotekoshi flood survivors
items.summary: Authorities are mapping unsafe settlements and considering safer locations, but past disasters show that moving communities away from their land and livelihoods can be unsuitable.

items.title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah to lead Nepali delegation to UN General Assembly
items.summary: Shah will take a small delegation to New York and make Nepal’s case on the Bhotekoshi disaster.

items.title: New bypass track to be built above collapsed Krishnabhir stretch
items.summary: Authorities race to restore Kathmandu’s main supply route as a 70-metre stretch plunged into the Trishuli river on Sunday. Engineers are also exploring long-term alternatives.

items.title: Bhotekoshi flood leaves Syafrubesi in ruins, cuts off road access
items.summary: Much of the settlement was swept away by the flood, while damaged roads have hampered relief, rescue and the search for people still missing.

items.title: EU provides additional Rs89 million in aid for Nepal flood victims
items.summary: The new funding will support up to 20,000 people in Bagmati Province with shelter, cash assistance, healthcare, water and sanitation services, and other emergency aid.

items.title: 114 Nepalis stranded in China return through Tatopani border
items.summary: The returnees were among 147 Nepali citizens stranded in China after devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi river on August 26, with more expected to cross the border in the coming days.
